description: ¡Somos un equipo de 6 estudiantes apasionados por la robótica, el diseño y la programación! Para el reto Navegador de misiones lunares CLPS, nuestro objetivo es ir más allá de una simple página web y desarrollar una experiencia interactiva que acerque la exploración lunar a más personas, despertando su curiosidad e interés por la ciencia y la tecnología.
summary:
# MOONVERSE: Lunar Exploration Within Everyone's Reach

MOONVERSE is an educational and interactive web application designed to bring knowledge about lunar exploration closer to students, educators, and the general public through an engaging and accessible experience. Its purpose is to make it easier to understand the main factors involved in selecting lunar landing sites and planning missions at the Moon's south pole.

The platform features five educational mini-games that allow users to progressively explore and understand challenges related to terrain safety, solar illumination, communication with Earth, operational time management, and satellite signal relaying. Upon completing these activities, users unlock a technical archive containing information about real lunar missions, connecting interactive learning with scientific and technological advances in space exploration.

The importance of MOONVERSE lies in reducing barriers to accessing scientific knowledge. In countries such as Ecuador, where these topics may receive limited exposure and can be difficult to understand without specialized knowledge, it is important to develop educational alternatives that spark curiosity and encourage interest in science and technology.
details:
MOONVERSE

What does it do and how does it work?

MOONVERSE is a first-person educational simulator focused on lunar south pole exploration. Players navigate a 3D lunar environment and complete five missions: selecting safe landing zones, comparing solar illumination, pointing an antenna toward Earth, organizing rover tasks according to operational windows, and finding a suitable position for a relay satellite. Each mission includes a storyline, instructions, and a scientific explanation. Progress is saved in the browser.

What are its benefits?

It allows users to learn concepts related to space exploration through visual and interactive experiences. The missions demonstrate how terrain, sunlight, communications, and available time can affect lunar operations. They also encourage users to compare data and make decisions rather than simply reading information.

What is the expected impact?

The project aims to spark interest in science and space exploration while helping students and the general public understand some of the challenges involved in planning lunar missions. Its scenarios are educational simulations: they do not replace real scientific data or serve as tools for actual landing planning.

What tools and technologies were used?

HTML was used to structure the pages, CSS for the visual design, and JavaScript for interactions and mission logic. Three.js generates and displays the 3D world in the browser. Progress is saved using localStorage. To run the project on Windows, a .bat file is included to launch a local server using Python. No specialized hardware is required, but a modern browser compatible with WebGL is needed, along with a keyboard and mouse for navigation.

What makes it creative?

It combines an explorable 3D world with a narrative-driven mini-game campaign. Characters guide players through connected missions, where decisions made in one activity prepare them for the next challenge. The terrain and several visual elements are procedurally generated through code, without relying on external 3D models.

What factors did the team consider?

The team considered clear instructions and controls, the gradual progression of missions, browser performance, and the ability to play without relying on external online services. Efforts were also made to ensure that the activities teach space exploration concepts without presenting the simulation as a real operational tool.
